newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines extends stay of North Korean defector.
newsitem.headline: Philippines extends stay of North Korean defector.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he had agreed to a joint request by South Korea and China to extend North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop's stay in the Philippines.

Ramos, citing security concerns, declined to say how long Hwang would remain in the country but Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Tuesday that Manila was considering allowing Pyongyang's top ideologue to stay for a month.
Hwang has been in a secret hideaway since China spirited him to the former U.S. Clark airbase north of Manila 16 days ago after he defected to the South Korean consulate in Beijing on February 12.
The Philippines was a joint choice of Seoul and Beijing as a third country transit point before Hwang, the most senior North Korean official to flee the Stalinist state, was flown to South Korea.

Ramos said his government had received "a request from South Korea, supported by the People's Republic of China", that the Philippines allow Hwang and aide, Kim Duk Hong, to stay "for an additional period of time".
"Upon the recommendation of the Department of Foreign Affairs, I have decided to respond positively to this request," Ramos said in a statement he read at his weekly news conference.
"We have made this decision in response to the request of two friendly neighbours," he said.

"We have done so in the same spirit that moved us to agree to their temporary stay in the Philippines, that is, out of our desire to help reduce tensions in the Korean peninsula, contribute to reconciliation among the Korean people, and do our part on behalf of peace and security in the region."
Ramos refused to elaborate, citing what he called "the sensitivity of this subject".

The government has shrouded Hwang's whereabouts under a veil of secrecy and kept a close watch on airports and seaports around the country due to fears that Hwang might be a target of Pyongyang hitmen.

Days after Hwang's defection, suspected Pyongyang agents shot dead prominent North Korean defector Li Il-nam near Seoul, despite plastic surgery on Li's face. Li was a nephew of the former wife of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.
Senior Philippine military sources said Hwang, 73, was under the protection of an elite presidential task force commanded by armed forces intelligence chief General Benjamin Libarnes.
